Every AWS security launch of 2026, week by week

All security, identity, governance and compliance announcements from the AWS What's New feed between week 1 and week {{W}} of 2026. Filter by pillar or service, pick a week to drill down, and read the architecture deep dive for week 40.
Giovanni - Sr. Geo Security Specialist SA, AWS WWSO LATAM
Weeks follow the ISO calendar (Monday to Sunday).
Launches per week, stacked by pillar. Select a bar to drill into that week.
Amazon GuardDuty: centralized enablement with AWS Organizations declarative policies
An organization policy now enables GuardDuty across every account and Region. The configuration applies to existing accounts and is maintained automatically as new accounts join.
Defined from the delegated administrator account
Organization root, OUs or individual accounts
Applies in every Region where GuardDuty is available
For Regions that need different enablement
Policy-set enablement cannot be changed from the GuardDuty console or API
Covered automatically when they join the organization
All commercial Regions and AWS GovCloud (US)
GuardDuty console → Organization policies, or the AWS Organizations APIs

Financial groups in Brazil and Mexico often run hundreds of accounts across several Regions. A single policy replaces per-Region enablement scripts and closes the drift that auditors find when a new account goes live without threat detection.
GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring is now included in the Security Hub Threat Analytics plan

Runtime Monitoring inspects operating system, network and file activity to surface container escapes, privilege escalation and cryptomining. Where Security Hub is enabled, this usage now bills under Security Hub instead of GuardDuty.
No separate GuardDuty charge for Runtime Monitoring in accounts and Regions with Security Hub enabled
One Security Hub usage type spanning EC2, EKS and ECS on Fargate
GuardDuty security agents, with no reconfiguration
Free trials: Threat Analytics and Essentials stay separate, no new trial
Teams that budget security tooling per service should check Cost Explorer or the Security Hub usage page this month: the line item moves from GuardDuty to Security Hub.
Identity Store APIs now accept resource ARNs in addition to resource IDs
Anywhere the Identity Store APIs took the ID of a user, group, group membership or identity store, they now also accept its ARN. The change is additive: existing integrations keep working.
Before: parse the ID out of the ARN
Provisioning pipelines that pass ARNs between CloudFormation, CDK and access-review tooling can drop their parsing step, which removes one more place for a joiner-mover-leaver flow to break.
AWS accounts now support phone number verification
Primary contact phone numbers were only checked for format. They can now be verified out of band with an SMS one-time passcode, in the console or through the API.
Call SendPhoneNumberVerification (or start from the console) to send a 6-digit OTP by SMS.
Changing the number with PutContactInformation asks for verification again.
Member accounts inherit verified status when they use the management account's number
Incident response plans depend on AWS reaching the right person. A verified primary contact is a quick hygiene item to add to account baselines across the organization.
IAM Identity Center extends multi-Region support to more AWS Regions

Identity Center can now be replicated to opt-in Regions, and between Regions inside AWS GovCloud (US) and the AWS China Regions. Before, replication covered only the enabled-by-default commercial Regions.
Identities, entitlements and settings copied automatically
Users keep account access with provisioned entitlements if the primary Region is disrupted
External IdP or Identity Center directory, organization instances
Identity Center is free; standard KMS charges apply
Mexico (Central) is an opt-in Region, so this launch is the one to watch for teams that want a replica close to Mexican users. Confirm it in the AWS Capabilities by Region list before planning.
CloudTrail Event Coverage uncovers blind spots in data plane logging

A new console experience shows, at account and organization level, which services and resource types have data event logging enabled and which do not, and lets you subscribe to the missing coverage from the same view.
Closing a gap from the CLI
When a regulator or auditor asks whether access to personal data is logged, the coverage view turns the answer into a checklist per service and resource type instead of a manual inventory.
Security Hub remediation plans prioritize and fix exposures by root cause

Remediation plans group exposure findings that share a root cause. Fixing the one underlying resource, such as a misconfigured setting or an overly permissive policy, resolves or lowers the severity of several exposures at once.
Plans can be consumed by AI agents and automation
The root cause, not the individual finding
No additional cost in Security Hub Essentials
Lean security teams can work a short list of root causes instead of a long list of findings, and keep the fixes as reviewed infrastructure as code.
AWS Continuum for Penetration Testing now in 6 more Regions

AWS Continuum for Penetration Testing (AWS Security Agent) is a managed service for penetration testing web applications and APIs. It now runs in Asia Pacific (Seoul), Canada (Montreal), Europe (London), US East (Columbus), Europe (Paris) and Europe (Stockholm).
Vulnerability assessment and evidence for frameworks such as PCI DSS and ISO 27001
Run tests close to production and meet data residency needs
South America (São Paulo) is not in this batch, but AWS Security Agent has been available there since July 1 (filter the explorer by AWS Security Agent to see it).
Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall with Palo Alto Networks Advanced DNS Security is GA

Security teams can detect and block malicious DNS traffic from their VPCs with PANW Advanced DNS Security rules, without deploying separate firewalls or changing VPC configuration. Generally available in 32 AWS Regions, after a preview that started in June.
Rule group with PANW Advanced DNS Security
Command-and-control, malware, phishing, newly registered domains
Associate a rule group with a VPC
Customers that already standardize on Palo Alto Networks on premises get the same DNS threat intelligence inside VPCs without inserting appliances into the traffic path.
DNS analytics and insights for Route 53 Global Resolver and DNS Firewall
Native CloudWatch integration gives visibility into DNS query patterns, DNS Firewall rule effectiveness and anomalous activity. A new Analytics tab in both consoles brings the views together.
Metrics, metric filters and Contributor Insights
Example: more than 10 blocked queries per VPC in one hour
Standard CloudWatch pricing for the metrics you opt in to
The PANW rules above: block and measure in the same service
An alarm on blocked queries per VPC gives SOC teams an early signal that a workload is reaching out to known-bad domains.
Amazon Kinesis Video Streams now supports VPC endpoints with AWS PrivateLink
Control plane, video ingestion and playback traffic stays on the AWS network through interface VPC endpoints, with no internet gateway, NAT device or public IP.
All Kinesis Video Streams Regions, including GovCloud (US) and China (Beijing)
Video from branches and ATMs often carries personal data. Keeping it off the public internet removes NAT and public IPs from the design and narrows the attack surface.
Actionable security posture recommendations in the Secrets Manager console
Secrets Manager now uses the AWS Recommended Actions framework to show tailored suggestions next to each secret.
Find secrets that need rotation configured.
Switch from the default service key to a customer managed KMS key.
Act on secret configuration improvements from a single view.
All Regions in the AWS partition where Secrets Manager is offered
Rotation and key ownership come up in almost every LGPD and financial-sector review. The console now points at the secrets that fall short.
S3 Object Lock variable retention with event holds now in AWS GovCloud (US)

Variable retention applies WORM protection to objects whose retention period starts with a future event, such as a contract closing or an audit completing. It launched in commercial Regions on September 8 and now reaches GovCloud (US-East) and GovCloud (US-West).
WORM while the hold is in place
Object kept for the specified duration
A legal hold ends protection on removal; an event hold starts the retention period

Record-keeping rules that count retention from the end of a contract or relationship fit this model directly, without keeping data longer than policy requires. In LATAM, use the commercial-Region launch from September 8.
AgentCore Gateway supports private TLS certificates for VPC endpoints

AgentCore Gateway now trusts TLS certificates signed by your own private certificate authority on MCP, OpenAPI and HTTP proxy targets, so agents connect to private endpoints in your VPC without an intermediate Application Load Balancer.
Calls a tool through the gateway
Trust anchor: your CA certificate (PEM) from S3 or Secrets Manager
Certificate issued by your private CA
Regions with both AgentCore Gateway and VPC Lattice
Banks wiring agents into internal credit, fraud or service APIs can keep their corporate PKI end to end instead of adding a load balancer just to terminate TLS.

Enforcement got harder to bypass (GuardDuty organization policies), visibility gaps got easier to see (CloudTrail Event Coverage, Secrets Manager recommendations, DNS analytics), and fixes got grouped by root cause (Security Hub remediation plans). For LATAM teams, the practical starting point is the GuardDuty policy plus remediation plans: a uniform detection baseline, then a short list of root causes to fix.
